About us

Luno is the crypto investment app you can rely on, enabling you to buy, store and explore crypto securely. We’re committed to putting the power of cryptocurrency in everyone's hands, sensibly and responsibly. Since 2013, we’ve helped millions of people around the world invest safely in crypto. We do this by cutting through the hype and supporting customers at every step of the way. All products and cryptocurrencies on our platform must first meet stringent legal, risk and technical security standards.

Transparency is key for us. Luno stores all crypto on a 1:1 basis and we have rigorous processes in place so you can be confident your investment is secure. We're available in multiple markets around the world and we work closely with regulators and other key stakeholders to ensure compliance with local laws, as we believe this is the best way to help everyone, everywhere, invest safely.

About the team:

You will report into Jeremy Jeesandaran, Head of Marketing (SEA) and be provided with an exciting opportunity to join a collaborative, cross-functional environment where marketing, compliance, and product teams work closely together to build community trust across Southeast Asia.

The role in a nutshell:

Build and Grow the Luno Community. Help Luno expand its presence across SEA markets through engaging online and offline community events, accessible educational content, and high-impact marketing campaigns. You will also support the growth of our Affiliate Marketing channel and assist with SEO implementation, learning firsthand how a regulated crypto exchange fosters trust and brings new users into the ecosystem.

Your mission will be:

- Drive Community Initiatives and Events:

  • Help plan and run online and in-person community events, including meetups, workshops, webinars, campus sessions, and AMAs.
  • Manage end-to-end event logistics covering venues, invitations, run-of-show, materials, and on-the-day support.
  • Explore and pitch new community initiatives, partnerships, and programmes that help everyday people understand crypto and Luno.
  • Monitor community channels to spot recurring questions, sentiment shifts, and emerging topics, flagging insights to the team.

- Execute Marketing Campaigns:

  • Support the design of marketing campaigns from initial concept and messaging through to channel planning and creative briefs.
  • Assist with campaign launches across channels, coordinating closely with design, content, and compliance teams for reviews.
  • Track campaign performance and share concise summaries of key learnings and recommendations for future iterations.

- Grow Affiliate Marketing:

  • Identify, reach out to, and onboard new affiliates—including content creators, communities, and education platforms—to expand Luno's affiliate channel.
  • Support existing affiliates with creative briefs, approved marketing materials, and timely responses to common inquiries.
  • Track affiliate performance, sign-ups, and payouts, flagging top performers and potential issues to the team.
  • Review affiliate content to ensure alignment with Luno's brand and compliance guidelines, escalating any non-compliance promptly.

- Support SEO Implementation:

  • Assist in implementing on-page SEO updates across Luno's website and educational content, including metadata, headings, internal links, and image alt text.
  • Help publish and update educational articles and landing pages with target keywords properly integrated.
  • Conduct routine SEO health checks (such as identifying broken links and page issues) and track keyword rankings and traffic for key pages.

A little about you:

- Must-Have Qualifications & Traits:

  • Education: Currently enrolled in, or recently graduated from, a degree or diploma in Communications, Marketing, Media, or a related field.
  • Language Proficiency: Strong written and spoken English and Bahasa Melayu; proficiency in Mandarin or other local languages is a plus.
  • Organisation & Reliability: Highly detail-oriented and organised, capable of juggling event logistics, campaign deadlines, and affiliate follow-ups simultaneously.
  • Creativity & Proactivity: Eager to bring fresh, practical ideas to the table for community initiatives, campaigns, and partnerships.
  • Analytical Comfort: Comfortable working with numbers to track performance in spreadsheets and summarise what the data shows.
  • Industry Curiosity: Genuine interest in crypto, fintech, or personal finance, paired with a willingness to learn fast in a regulated environment.

- Nice to Have:

  • Experience organising events, campus activities, or community programmes.
  • Basic familiarity with SEO or web analytics tools (such as Google Analytics, Search Console, or similar).
  • Prior experience with affiliate, influencer, or partnership outreach.
  • Experience moderating or managing a community, social page, or Discord/Reddit group.
  • Basic design or content editing skills (e.g., Canva, Higgsfield, or similar tools).

How to Apply?

Apply through Luno's careers page. Include your CV and a short note on why you'd be a great fit for building Luno's community. Links to any decks, events, campaigns, videos, or community work you've done are welcome but not required. Shortlisted candidates may be asked to complete a short take-home task.

What you will gain:

  • Hands-on experience running community engagement for a global crypto exchange across three platforms.
  • A public on-camera portfolio of explainer videos.
  • Exposure to how brand, compliance and community teams work together in a regulated industry.

Life at Luno:

  • Remote but reachable work policy gives you the freedom to choose between working from home or the office.
  • A collaborative, friendly work community, with regular social events and virtual cooking, dancing, drawing and house planting classes hosted by our Lunauts
  • Free lunch and snacks

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

To help support that mission, in August we announced that Stripe had agreed to acquire OpenRouter, a leading AI model gateway and routing platform. While that acquisition is under regulatory review and has not yet closed, our intent is that this role will support the OpenRouter team following the closing of the acquisition.

About the team

OpenRouter helps developers and businesses access and use a broad range of AI models through a unified platform. This role sits at the intersection of OpenRouter and Stripe, supporting hiring across Tech, GTM, and Core teams. You’ll serve as a bridge between the 2 organizations, bringing Stripe’s recruiting standards, talent networks, and resources to OpenRouter while protecting its speed and minimizing operational overhead.

You’ll align to Tech, GTM, or Core, but you won’t be dedicated to a single job profile within that function. For example, a GTM Recruiter may support Sales, Solutions Architecture, Marketing, or other GTM roles as priorities shift. The same model applies across Tech and Core.

What you’ll do

Own full-cycle recruiting for your aligned function, moving across job profiles based on business priority, from intake and market mapping through offer acceptance and onboarding handoff. You’ll combine direct execution with consultative partnership, working closely with hiring managers to clarify needs, advise on talent markets, build and engage qualified pipelines, and move candidates through structured, timely processes.

You’ll operate with startup speed while leveraging Stripe’s infrastructure and reach. You’ll use metrics to identify risk and guide action, while keeping recruiting outcomes, not reporting or process for its own sake, at the center of the work.

Responsibilities

  • Own full-cycle recruiting across the full range of roles within your aligned function, Tech, GTM, or Core, moving between job profiles as business priorities shift
  • Build qualified and inclusive pipelines through hands-on sourcing across communities, referrals, events, market mapping, relationship-based outreach, and other creative channels beyond inbound applications and standard LinkedIn outreach
  • Partner consultatively with hiring managers to translate business priorities into clear role requirements, search strategies, structured assessments, and timely decisions
  • Use funnel metrics, market evidence, and candidate feedback to identify risks, recommend actions, and communicate progress without allowing reporting or process to substitute for recruiting
  • Deliver a thoughtful candidate experience and maintain relationships with prospective candidates for immediate and future needs
  • Serve as an operational bridge between OpenRouter and Stripe by absorbing coordination where possible, maintaining continuity, and reducing the time OpenRouter leaders spend navigating recruiting processes
  • Flex across job profiles within your aligned function when priorities shift or additional coverage is needed

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, including direct ownership of sourcing, assessment, stakeholder partnership, and closing
  • Experience recruiting in a high-growth technology startup, preferably during a stage below 200 employees
  • Demonstrated recruiting depth in at least 1 of the following areas: Tech, GTM, or Core, with experience recruiting across multiple job profiles or clear evidence you can move between profiles as business priorities shift.
  • Demonstrated interest in and ability to personally conduct hands-on sourcing and build qualified pipelines through creative channels beyond inbound applications and standard LinkedIn outreach
  • Experience partnering consultatively with hiring managers, managing multiple searches, and using recruiting metrics and market evidence to identify risk and guide action
  • Ability to work through ambiguity, adapt quickly as priorities change, and balance direct execution with longer-term pipeline building

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience recruiting across both startup and larger-company environments and helping teams work effectively across different operating models
  • Experience supporting structured, competency-based hiring processes
  • Experience recruiting across multiple geographies or advising on location strategy
  • Practical experience using recruiting technology, talent intelligence, or AI tools to improve sourcing and candidate experience

The OKX Card Team builds the payment infrastructure connecting digital assets to global commerce. Partnering with major card networks like Visa and Mastercard, we power the OKX crypto card platform. Our team handles the full card lifecycle and payment stack—from instant issuance and real-time transaction authorization (Auth) to settlement, ledger management, and card growth engines.   • Exposure to cloud-native stacks (Docker, Kubernetes, AWS/GCP).
  • Professional working proficiency in both English and Mandarin (verbal and written) to effectively communicate with Mandarin-speaking stakeholders and review Chinese-language business documents.

In addition to the salary, a performance bonus and long-term incentives may be provided as part of the compensation package, as well as a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position offered. Our consumer business provides digital solutions for customers to better spend, borrow, invest, and save. Across Wealth Management, our growth is driven by a relentless focus on our people, our clients and customers, and leading-edge technology, data and design.


Goldman Sachs Private Bank

Goldman Sachs Private Bank provides competitive borrowing and cash management solutions from Goldman Sachs Bank USA that are strategically integrated with our client’s wealth management goals. Our experienced team partners with PWAs to advise clients on new loans, refinancing and restructuring of existing loans along with overall liability management. Our lenders and mortgage specialists provide a wide range of creative borrowing solutions against asset classes ranging from marketable securities and alternative investments, residential and commercial real estate to more tailored solutions against private assets such as aviation, fine art or vineyards. All team members are employees of Goldman Sachs Bank, USA


Private Lending Underwriting

Private Lending Underwriting (PLU), based in Bengaluru, is primarily responsible for the underwriting of loans to GS Private Wealth Management (PWM) clients. In this capacity, PLU assesses, underwrites, documents, and monitors the credit and business risks incurred in loan transactions. The underwriting process includes a thorough analysis of the borrower’s financial condition, assessment of any collateral securing the loan, identification of risks and mitigants, among other items. Types of loans underwritten include commercial real estate, GS and third-party private equity/hedge funds (including co-invest facilities), aircraft, fine art, hobby properties, private company stock, yachts, marketable securities, etc.
PLU also ensures that the underwriting standards approved by the bank are adhered to in the loan approval process, with exceptions appropriately mitigated and documented. In addition, PLU participates in various business-related initiatives, such as new product development and systems/operational enhancements.

Job Summary and Responsibilities

  • Interact with banking regulators on an as needed basis. Provide other support of GS Bank USA’s loan portfolio as requested
  • Foster strong communication with Regional Underwriting and Private Lending teams, Credit Risk Management, PWM teams, clients and GS Bank USA personnel

  • CPA or CFA a plus
  • 1-3 years of work experience in a financial field (mortgage or insurance underwriting is not relevant for this role)
  • Relevant work experience in commercial banking and/or private banking underwriting or credit roles

Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Role

Serve as the on-duty commander for Alpaca's most critical incidents, directing cross-functional response to restore service quickly, keeping the right people engaged and informed, and making sure every incident leaves behind something the organisation can act on.

You do not fix the outage. You make the response reliable: correct severity, the right engineers in the room, mitigation that does not stall, leaders informed in time, and follow-up work that survives the call.

Things You Get To Do

  • Command incidents end to end. Take command from declaration to mitigation, keeping responders focused on stopping customer and partner impact as fast as possible. Run the bridge, keep observers out of the responders' way, and name a stall out loud when you see one.
  • Classify and hold the line on severity. Set severity at declaration and re-check it as facts arrive. Risk advises on financial and regulatory materiality; the call is yours.
  • Engage the right people, fast. Identify the owning team by service, symptom and blast radius, page them, and expand the responder set the moment the first team is wrong or not enough. When a page goes unanswered, escalate - and escalate the escalation. Bring in the leaders who must make business calls: feature flags, traffic shedding, failover, freeze-or-ship.
  • Hold the bridge, and protect the people fixing it. Keep engineering and technical support uninterrupted - questions from stakeholders, partners and executives come to you. Be the single source of truth to the partner communications team on impact, severity and timing: you decide when a status page update or partner contact is needed, they write and send it, and chasing a late or stale update is yours.
  • Run follow-the-sun handoffs. Deliver warm, high-fidelity handoffs across regions: current impact and severity, mitigation path and next actions, who is in the room, outstanding decisions, and what must not be dropped. The incoming commander confirms ownership before you step away - command never goes dark at a region boundary.
  • Close the loop, on the clock. Maintain the timeline of facts as the incident runs rather than reconstructing it afterwards - in a regulated business that record has to hold up long after the call ends. Once mitigated, make sure a blameless retrospective is scheduled with a named owner and a timebox, and record where the cause sits - that choice sets which follow-up items are mandatory. Every action item needs a real ticket, one named accountable, a priority and a category, delivered inside the agreed service level. If a postmortem produces nothing but low-priority items, treat that as a signal the analysis stopped early and escalate to SRE rather than passing it on.
  • Automate the coordination away. Coordination is the part of this job that should eventually belong to a machine. Every manual prompt you send - the update that is due, the question nobody answered, the partner nobody contacted - is a candidate for automation, and the direction we are heading is AI handling the routine so commanders can spend their attention on judgement. You get us there by working to the decision trees, saying where they are wrong, and being honest about which of your instincts are actually rules.

Who You Are (Must-Haves)

  • 4+ years commanding or co-commanding high-severity incidents in a production engineering, SRE or technical operations environment.
  • You direct technical responders under pressure without being the person writing the fix.
  • You make and defend crisp severity and escalation decisions, and you take charge without waiting to be asked. Command means waking senior people at 03:00, interrupting an executive, and telling an experienced engineer to stop what they are doing - with an audience watching. It is a visible, directive role and it needs to be instinctive.
  • You can read a dashboard and judge for yourself whether impact has actually stopped.
  • You communicate clearly with engineers, executives and partner-facing stakeholders - and you know the difference between briefing the comms function and speaking for the company.
  • You are comfortable holding other teams to account in the moment, across a reporting line that is not yours, without turning it into friction.
  • You thrive in a follow-the-sun model with clean cross-region handoffs.
  • You understand FinTech concepts and the trust stakes of API-driven financial platforms.
  • You use AI tools and agentic automation to reduce manual toil and speed up response.
  • You will work a regional coverage window as part of a global 24x7 Incident Commander roster.

Who You Might Be (Nice-to-Haves)

  • Formal incident command training - ITIL, Major Incident Management or crisis management.
  • Experience with modern incident management and on-call platforms.
  • You have written severity rubrics, decision trees, escalation matrices, runbooks or incident playbooks.
  • You have commanded in game days, tabletop exercises or incident simulations, not only in production.
  • You have partnered with problem management or reliability programme functions to roadmap incident follow-ups.
  • Online securities trading or capital markets experience, or another regulated, market-hours-sensitive domain.

How We Take Care of You:

  • Competitive Salary & Stock Options
  • Health Benefits
  • New Hire Home-Office Setup: One-time USD $500
  • Monthly Stipend: USD $150 per month via a Brex Card

WHO WE ARE

Baton Corporation builds and maintains pump.fun — the dominant memecoin launchpad, processing $300M+ in daily volume. Last year, pump.fun generated over $500M in profit with a team of fewer than 100 people.

We ship to production daily. Bureaucracy is minimal. We solve hard technical and go-to-market problems at scale, and we're data-driven — systematic tools and the scientific method decide what works, not opinions.

Working with us isn't for everyone. We work in person. Hours are long and sometimes strange. The pace is intense. Individuals own their function end to end. When we ship a change, it reaches hundreds of thousands of users within days.

 

THE ROLE

We're making a founding hire: a Staff Data Scientist in Marketing Science to own the mathematics behind our paid growth - the causal measurement, the response curves, the customer-value models and the optimisation that decide where our multi-million-dollar, always-on acquisition budget goes across Google, Apple Search Ads, OpenAI ads, Meta, TikTok and X. There is no inherited methodology - you design it from first principles.

Your job is to answer one question, continuously and with evidence: where should the next $1 million go to generate the most additional profit - and how confident are we?

This is a hands-on, builder role. You'll write the models yourself, design the experiments that keep them honest, and sit next to the people moving the budget. Our data engineers own the pipelines; you own the science.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Build our marketing measurement system - a Bayesian marketing mix model with adstock and saturation, channel-level response curves and full uncertainty, in PyMC, Stan, NumPyro, Meridian or a framework you can defend
  • Separate attributed from incremental - design and analyse geo-experiments, conversion-lift tests, holdouts and synthetic-control studies, and use the results to calibrate the model
  • Turn models into budget decisions - estimate marginal ROAS and marginal CAC by channel, run constrained budget optimisation and give the paid acquisition team a clear, risk-aware allocation every planning cycle
  • Model what a user is worth - build LTV, retention and payback models tied to activation and trading activity, so we optimise for profit, not platform-reported ROAS
  • Measure what the platforms can't - build defensible approaches for newer or opaque channels (OpenAI ads, X, Apple Search Ads, crypto-native networks) where lift tooling is thin or missing
  • Work alongside the Head of Paid Acquisition & Performance Marketing to set test roadmaps, define success metrics and decide what to scale and what to stop
  • Ship production-quality code - versioned, tested and reproducible - and partner with Data Engineering on the inputs the models need
  • Explain uncertainty plainly - write decision memos that founders and operators can act on, including when the right answer is "we don't know yet - here's the test"

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • Advanced quantitative training - a PhD, MSc or equivalent depth in mathematics, statistics, econometrics, physics or operations research. What matters is that you can derive it, not just run it
  • 4+ years of hands-on experience (PhD research counts), with a track record building marketing mix or advertising response models that moved real budgets - in-house at a consumer, fintech or app business, or at a measurement company (Recast, Haus, PyMC Labs, Google, Meta or similar) - with results you can explain and evidence
  • Hands-on causal inference - you have designed, run and analysed incrementality experiments, and you know what to do when the experiment and the model disagree• Deep Bayesian modelling - hierarchical models, priors you can justify, identification, posterior diagnostics and the computational know-how to make them fit at speed
  • Strong Python or R in production - you write the model code yourself
  • Commercial judgment - you think natively in incremental profit, LTV, CAC and payback, and you can turn a posterior into a recommendation a non-specialist will act on
  • A scrappy, high-energy operator mindset - you thrive in a fast-paced, resource-lean environment where you're building the playbook as you go

NICE TO HAVE

  • Contributions to open-source measurement tools - PyMC-Marketing, Meridian, Robyn, LightweightMMM, CausalPy, Stan, GeoLift or similar
  • Mobile app user acquisition - SKAdNetwork, AppsFlyer or Adjust, and Apple Search Ads
  • Crypto experience - as a retail trader, or through work at a crypto startup or larger crypto company

Sophisticated equations matter. Better allocation decisions matter more.

HOW WE'LL MEASURE SUCCESS

  • First 30 days: Current measurement audited, a baseline response model live for core channels, and the first incrementality tests designed with the paid acquisition team
  • First 90 days: An experiment-calibrated model producing channel response curves, marginal returns and a recommended allocation with confidence ranges, used in the budget cycle
  • First 180 days: Budget reallocations driven by the model delivering measurable incremental profit, with an always-on test-and-learn programme across existing and new channels

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

  • Base salary: $300,000 - $400,000, depending on experience and scope
  • Performance-related compensation: Generous performance bonus; token participation depending on level
  • Benefits and relocation support: To be confirmed for this role

LOCATION & ELIGIBILITY

  • New York preferred, working in person with our growth team. For exceptional candidates we will consider remote work with strong overlap with US Eastern hours and regular time in New York.
  • For New York-based roles you must be authorized to work in the United States. Please tell us in your application whether you will now or in the future require visa sponsorship.

Send your résumé and a short example of a model or experiment that changed how advertising budget was spent: the question, your approach, and what moved. Links to papers, talks or code are welcome. No cover letter needed.
